Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

too little adverb and noun

also not enough, too few, not … enough, insufficiently

classical

Aug. Conf. 10.31.44: dēlectātiōnī parum est
Cic. Brut. 240: leporis parum (Lewis & Short)

parum

indeclinable noun and adverb; as a noun with a genitive

too little, not enough

Lewis & Short: the opposite of satis and nimium; it has no comparative of its own (minus, minimē). With a genitive, too little of: frondis parum; with an adjective or a verb, “not … enough”: parum cautī, not careful enough.

Other words

  • nōn satis — not enough

    adverb with its negative · also used · classical · Mart. 14.220.1: nōn satis est ars sōla cocō; Liv. praef. 1: nec satis sciō

    Plainly “not enough”, without the reproach of parum (see enough).

Examples

  • nam quod salūtī satis est, dēlectātiōnī parum est

    for what is enough for health is too little for pleasureAug. Conf. 10.31.44

  • hoc lautum est parum; illud rēctē: iterum sīc mementō

    this one hasn’t been rinsed enough; that one’s right: remember to do it that way againTer. Ad. 425–426

  • cūr frondis parum est, strāmenta dēsunt?

    why is there too little fodder, and no straw?Phaedr. 2.8.22

  • nōn quī parum habet, sed quī plūs cupit, pauper est

    the poor man is not the one who has too little, but the one who wants moreSen. Ep. 2.6

  • mātūtīna parum cautōs jam frīgora mordent

    the morning cold is already biting those who are not careful enoughHor. S. 2.6.45

  • nōn satis est ars sōla cocō

    skill alone is not enough for a cookMart. 14.220.1

  • satis ēloquentiae, sapientiae parum

    eloquence enough, too little wisdomSall. Cat. 5.4

See also enough, too, less, a little.
